relevance_note: Evidence review whose Table 1 summarizes individual previously published GAMT deficiency patients (early-treated infants and their later-treated older siblings) with ages and outcomes: "Six studies describing 8 infants were identified by the evidence review".
method_note: Newborn-screening evidence review; the only individual-level data are in Table 1 (literature summary). Table 1 has no patient label column, so each row's early-treated infant is 'Table 1 row k' (k = 1-9 counting data rows) and the sibling in the 'Sibling With Later Treatment' columns is 'older sibling of Table 1 row k' (relation from the header 'Age of Older Sibling at Diagnosis'; sex never stated). Row 6 (Viau et al, 2013) has '—' in the sibling columns, defined in the table notes as 'no sibling comparator', so no sibling row. 17 people in total. The Source cell is copied to source_reference_in_review. 'Age of Diagnosis and Treatment' is recorded as age at diagnosis (it is one combined column); 'Duration of Treatment and Follow-up' is a duration, not an age, so it goes in treatment_summary and age at last evaluation is not reported. Treatment content (creatine, ornithine etc.) is described only generally in the text, not per person, so not attributed. 'Developmental Outcome at Follow-up: Normal' is recorded under D-27 as developmental delay excluded and the checklist item 'developmental delay or intellectual disability' excluded; this is a judgement that a normal developmental outcome rules out both. 'Speech and fine motor delays' and 'cognitive impairment' were taken as observed for 'developmental delay or intellectual disability'; 'speaks “a few words”' as observed limited speech; 'improved autistic features' as autistic features observed (had them). 'improved tone' and 'Improved motor skills, started walking' were not converted to hypotonia or motor delay (type of tone abnormality not stated). Possible contradiction / duplication: rows 1 (El-Gharbawy et al, 2013^17) and 2 (Dhar et al, 2009^6) have identical cells (Prenatal, 42 mo, Normal, 10 mo, 6.5 y, Speech and fine motor delays), and the text says 'Six studies describing 8 infants' and 'Seven of the 8 reported infants had normal developmental outcomes' while Table 1 has 9 rows (8 Normal). The paper does not say two rows are the same person, so they were kept as separate rows; a downstream merge should check. No GAMT variant is printed or attributed to any person, so the variants table is empty. Group counts (Utah 1 case, New York 1 case, Australia 1 case, 22-subject study, Viau 5 patients) give no individual-level facts and get no rows. n_patients_reported left null: the text's '8 infants' excludes the siblings and no total of described patients is stated; cohort_size_as_stated null. is_proband null for all (no proband/index wording). The output was built by a short Python script that splits the Table 1 rows; each cell assignment was checked against the table by hand.
